evidence: Zheng et al. describe Market-1501 as a person re-identification benchmark containing 1,501 identities collected using six cameras.
source: Zheng et al. 2015, Scalable Person Re-Identification: A Benchmark
rationale: The benchmark purpose and collection setting are explicitly documented.
supported_analysis: Analysis of the documented collection context and benchmark purpose
unsupported_analysis: Claims about participant circumstances not described in the reviewed sources

evidence: The reviewed original paper and attribute documentation do not establish participant consent, refusal, opt-out, or withdrawal procedures.
source: Zheng et al. 2015; Lin et al. 2019; Market-1501 Attribute repository
rationale: Consent and autonomy procedures could not be established from the reviewed sources.
supported_analysis: Documentation-gap analysis concerning consent and autonomy
unsupported_analysis: Claim that consent definitely was or was not obtained

evidence: The dataset links observations to persistent person identities across cameras, while the reviewed sources do not clearly document anonymization, redaction, or comparable privacy safeguards.
source: Zheng et al. 2015; Lin et al. 2019; Market-1501 Attribute repository
rationale: Identifiability is documented, but privacy safeguards are incompletely documented.
supported_analysis: Analysis of documented identity linkage and privacy limitations
unsupported_analysis: Claim that comprehensive privacy protections were provided

evidence: The official attribute repository provides 27 hand-annotated attributes at identity level for 751 training and 750 test identities, including age and gender categories.
source: Lin et al. 2019; Market-1501 Attribute repository
rationale: The categories, annotation unit, and manual annotation provenance are documented.
supported_analysis: Analysis of the released age and gender annotation distributions
unsupported_analysis: Claims that age is verified chronological age or gender is self-identified gender

evidence: Documented identity-level age and gender annotations support representation analysis, but the reviewed evidence does not provide verified demographic ground truth or group-linked model fairness outcomes.
source: Lin et al. 2019; Market-1501 Attribute repository
rationale: The available evidence supports limited representation questions but not broader demographic or performance-fairness claims.
supported_analysis: Representation analysis of the released annotations
unsupported_analysis: Verified demographic fairness or group-performance fairness claims

evidence: The dataset and attribute resources are publicly described for research use, but the reviewed sources do not clearly establish a complete set of downstream access, redistribution, and lifecycle controls.
source: Zheng et al. 2015; Market-1501 Attribute repository
rationale: Some access context is documented, but comprehensive downstream-use governance is not established.
unsupported_analysis: Claims about comprehensive downstream-use permissions or restrictions

evidence: The reviewed sources do not establish participant withdrawal, correction, removal, deprecation, or dataset lifecycle procedures.
source: Zheng et al. 2015; Lin et al. 2019; Market-1501 Attribute repository
rationale: Lifecycle-management procedures could not be established from the reviewed sources.
unsupported_analysis: Claim that a withdrawal or lifecycle mechanism exists or does not exist
